findings.title: Hung/dead flusher processes are never killed because isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process fails for SpawnProcess
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive` now only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.context.Process` (which is what `multiprocessing.Process` refers to), so the isinstance check is False and `kill()` is never invoked. Previously `self.process.kill()` was called unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher process is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is left running while a new process for the same shards is spawned, leading to leaked processes and two flushers concurrently flushing the same Redis shards (duplicate produces to buffered-segments). The same faulty check at line 346 means `terminate()` is never called in `join()` either. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: join() breaks out of the loop on deadline, skipping terminate() for remaining processes
findings.body: In `join()`, when the deadline has passed the loop does `break` before reaching `process.terminate()` for the current and all remaining processes. The inner `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or deadline > time.time())` already handles the deadline, so the early `break` only serves to skip termination. Any flusher processes still alive after the timeout are therefore left running after the strategy is joined (e.g. on rebalance), rather than being terminated as the single-process version did. Remove the early break (or move terminate before it).

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: `test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the top, and then later calls `time.sleep(0.1)` with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change". Since the module-level `time.sleep` attribute is patched, this call does nothing, so the test does not actually give the flusher thread any time; it merely relies on `step.join()` blocking until the thread finishes. Either the comment is misleading or the intended wait is not happening. Use a real sleep (e.g. bind `from time import sleep` before patching, as test_flusher.py does) or remove the line and comment.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `{"shards": shard_tag}` while the adjacent `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `{"shard": shard_tag}`. This makes dashboards/queries across flusher metrics inconsistent and is likely a typo. Also note `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of shards (e.g. "0,1,2"), so the `shard` tag no longer identifies a single shard, unlike the `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` metric which is emitted per individual shard.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is defined but never called anywhere in the module or tests; restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards` directly from `_ensure_processes_alive`. Dead code adds maintenance burden and may confuse readers into thinking per-shard restarts are supported. Remove it.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled into flusher PR
findings.body: The CLAUDE.md edit (adding a hasattr vs isinstance anti-pattern) is unrelated to the multiprocessed flusher change described in the PR. Bundling unrelated changes makes review and potential reverts harder; it should be a separate PR.
